title: Recognize and construct the phase-linear XOR flat signing at its exact scope
statement: For distinct nonzero XOR generators g_i in F2^k, solve a_i.g_i=0 and a_i.g_j+a_j.g_i=1 for i!=j. Then s_{x,x+g_i}=(-1)^(a_i.x) is undirected, Ui^2=I and UiUj=-UjUi, so A_s^2=d I and normsqrt(d)<2sqrt(d-1) for d>=3. Solubility iff Q(w)=sum_(i<j)wi wj vanishes on ker G, G=[g_i]; check BOTH Q on kernel basis vectors and pairwise polarisations, or solve the phase equations directly by polynomial GF2 elimination. This is only the phase-linear flat criterion, not necessary for ordinary sharp signability. Explicit16-vertex example: generators e0,e1,e2,e3,1111; basis-edge phases sum_(j<i)x_j and last phase x0+x2. Unsigned spectrum{5^1,1^10,(-3)^5} is Ramanujan/nonbipartite, signed square5I has +/-sqrt5 each8, and its32-vertex2lift is connected Ramanujan. Under the ADDITIONAL connected unsigned Ramanujan promise this flat subclass has the absolute bound in the next unit; it is not an infinite sparse promised-base family.
